title: Lech's multiplicity conjecture
main_claim: For every flat local homomorphism (R,m)->(S,n) of nonzero Noetherian local rings, e(R) <= e(S), with no restriction on dimension, residue fields or characteristic. The key new input is a uniform estimate (Thm 2.1): take a free complex of length h with alternating rank 0, contractible off V(I), whose entries lie in I^s, and an additive length lambda under which z behaves as a parameter system. Then lambda(H_0 F) >= lambda(C/I) s^h (b_0 - A_h sum b_i / s).

issues.location: sections/mixed.tex, proof of Thm 6.3, 'Finite extensions that make the differentials deep' (eq. mixed-deep-entries)
issues.description: The proof needs genuine membership b D ⊆ (z)^{q-h} D in a finite domain extension D. It gets this from Heitmann's mixed-characteristic Briançon–Skoda theorem as stated in [HeitmannMa, Prop 2.8]. Some versions of that theorem give only extended plus closure (epf) membership, which holds up to p^epsilon multipliers, and that would not be enough here. I could not check from the cited sources that the version used gives exact membership in R^+ under the stated hypothesis (p in the radical of the first generators, made automatic by putting p^a first in the list). If only the epf form holds, the lower bound (mixed-lower-bound) needs extra work.
issues.evidence: mixed.tex lines 211-232: 'its conclusion sends each element integral over I^{n+k'}=I^q into I^{k'+1}=I^{q-h} after an integral extension.' Everything later in the mixed-characteristic case depends on this exact containment.

coverage:
Read every section of the paper.
- Thm 2.1, line by line: the Koszul splitting and acyclicity modulo length zero; the graded comparison gr_I C ≅ (C/I)[Z] modulo length zero, derived from the total length a^h·mu; the twist-map nullhomotopy lemma via Čech filtration steps; the geometric and Koszul tower image identification giving chi_lambda(F_Y)=lambda H_0(F); twist invariance and chi(F_Y ⊗ V) = rank(V)·chi.
- The Eisenbud–Schreyer root bundle: cohomology degree v(a) = #{r_j > a} and chi = prod(a - r_j).
- The degree bounds that put H(G⊗V) in degree 0: for l>=0 at most i-1 roots exceed l-is, for l<0 at least i-1 do.
- The Rolle root placement and the Riemann-sum leading term: ∫_{-i}^0 H'/h = (H(0)-H(-i))/h = (h-1)!, which isolates b_0.
- Length inputs: the char-p perfection conductor and trace argument, the kernel bound O(1/q), and e_HK = e for parameter ideals. The mixed-characteristic CLMST inputs were taken as cited.
- Reductions and the Cohen-factorization setup: perfectness of J, equidimensionality, complete intersection or regular generic local rings.
- The char-p sum via Hilbert–Kunz associativity and Ma's identity.
- The mixed-characteristic upper bound: Lemma 6.1, both parts of Lemma 6.2, the multilinear power rule via cones, the order of the two limits, and coefficient-one counting through generic regularity.
- The char-0 finite free reduction, the polynomial certificate (source rank lower bound via the reduction relation, target Hilbert-function upper bound via monic initial relations), and the Artin approximation and specialization argument.
Not independently re-verified: the cited results Ma Lemma 4.2, CLMST Cor 4.0.4 / Prop 4.0.10 / Cor 4.0.18, Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem, Heitmann–Ma Prop 2.8, Kurano–Shimomoto.
